title: “XR for Cultural Heritage” session at EuroXR 2026
content:
ECHOES Sister Projects will participate ECHOES Sister Projects will participate in the “XR for Cultural Heritage” Session which will take place during EuroXR 2026, in Valencia, Spain, from the 3rd to the 6th November 2026.

This session will bring together several ECHOES Sister Projects to showcase their work, exchange experiences and strengthen collaboration among European initiatives working at the intersection of  eXtended Reality (XR), immersive technologies and Cultural Heritage.

The projects currently confirmed to participate are:

  • MusicSphere
  • EXCALIBUR
  • UNICHE
  • MNEME

    • The current programme consist of two dedicated sessions:

  • Wednesday, 4th November 2026 (11:30–12:30): Pitch session focused on dissemination, networking and increasing the visibility of the participating projects within the XR community.
  • Thursday, 5th November 2026 (15:00–16:30): Technical workshop dedicated to presenting ongoing developments, technologies, use cases and project results.

title: Eight new ECCCH Sister Projects start
content:
Following the Call for Innovative Use Cases for the Cultural Heritage Cloud (HORIZON-CL2-2025-01-HERITAGE-03), ECHOES is delighted to welcome eight more Sister Projects.

CULTUR-ACT – Collaborative Use Case Living Labs Fostering Tools and ResoURces Validation and Adoption in the European Cloud for Next-Gen Digital Heritage Communities Cooperation

CULTURAL.ACT is designed as a real-world proving ground for the ECCCH, leveraging on a community of CHIs and CCIs – of diverse types, cultural heritage domains, disciplines, size and expertise – that agree to collaborate and share experiences in the use of ECCCH tools and resources in core tasks of their own processes and working environments.

HERITWIN – Cultural Heritage Digital Twins

HERITWIN strengthens Europe’s cultural resilience by validating the European Collaborative Cloud for Cultural Heritage (ECCCH) through five real large-scale pilots in Sweden, Norway, Spain, The UK (Northern Ireland), and Greece. The project advances semantic digital twins, eXtended Reality reconstructions, preparedness modelling tools to support conservation, education, public engagement, tourism, and interoperable European data spaces.

title: COLOURS Community of Practice launched on LinkedIn
content:
Preserving art and cultural objects is deeply personal work. Whether you are dealing with fading pigments on an 18th-century polychrome sculpture, aged varnish on a canvas, or restoring historical film, the core question remains: how do we make the most precise, respectful decision for the object?

This group is an open meeting point for the people doing that work. It brings together conservator-restorers, museum curators, heritage scientists and creative tech developers to share daily studio challenges, test digital tools and discuss practical approaches to heritage preservation.

What happens in this group:

Real studio conversations: Open exchange on diagnostic data, colour management and real-world restoration bottlenecks.

Early tool access: Direct invitations to test open-source tools (such as 3D digital twins, predictive light-fading models and multi-layered diagnostic overlays) on real workflows.

Behind-the-scenes case studies: Updates from European conservation projects, from the Bratislava City Gallery altarpieces to photographic archives.

Funding and matchmaking: News on our upcoming €60,000 cascade funding grants for external pilot projects and a space to find project partners.

title: ECHOES at ENCATC Projects Showcase
content:
ECHOES will feature in the ENCATC Congress Projects Showcase Session 2026 with a presentation entitled “A Community-Centred Path to a Sustainable Cultural Heritage Cloud”.

The Showcase will take place as part of the ENCATC Congress in Nice, France, on the 23rd September 2026 under the theme “Artists and Cultural & Creative Professionals at the Centre: Rethinking Work, Policy, and Cultural Ecosystems“. The session offers a unique opportunity to present work to an international audience of educators, researchers, artists, cultural practitioners and policymakers, and to engage participants with the Cultural Heritage Cloud.

The presentation will be given jointly by Claudio Prandoni (ARIADNE) and Sophie Döppen (University of Antwerp) and is structured as follows:

  • Why start from communities?A brief introduction explaining that the success of the ECCCH depends not only on the technical infrastructure, but also on whether heritage communities adopt it and integrate it into their daily practice.

content: Agiatis Benardou, the President of the Board of Directors of DARIAH, delivered a keynote speech at the 2nd IEEE International Conference on Cyber Humanities (IEEE CH 2026). title: E-RIHS and Università Telematica Pegaso join the ECHOES consortium
content:
ECHOES is pleased to announce that E-RIHS has joined the ECHOES consortium as a beneficiary along with the Università Telematica Pegaso who has joined as an affiliated entity of ENCATC.

E-RIHS ERIC (European Research Infrastructure for Heritage Science) is the European legal consortium dedicated to advancing heritage science. It offers physical access to state-of-the-art facilities and resources, with data-driven research approaches, enabling the coordinated use of fixed and mobile analytical instruments, archives, reference collections, and digital tools, all supported by specialised training. For ECHOES, E-RIHS is responsible for long-term sustainability, bringing the interdisciplinary heritage science community’s contribution into the field.

title: SSH Open Marketplace training series session for GLAMS featuring ECHOES
content:
DARIAH is organising a session dedicated to GLAM audiences on Friday, the 18th of September where ECHOES will be prominently featured by Giorgia Lo Nigro from CNRS. This is as part of the 2026 SSH Open Marketplace training series.

Cultural heritage collections held by galleries, libraries, archives and museums (GLAM) are a cornerstone of arts and humanities research — but working with them brings its own data challenges, from fragmented standards to the gap between “metadata” and the real workflows researchers need to reuse this material responsibly.

This session is part of the SSH Open Marketplace Training Series 2026, an eight-part series of online hands-on workshops organised by the SSH Open Marketplace Editorial Board to strengthen FAIR and digital research competencies, following the FAIR-by-design methodology developed in skills4EOSC. This sixth session, “Thematic: GLAM institutions,” brings together speakers from the ECHOES project, the SSH Open Marketplace and ETH Zurich Library to look at cultural heritage and GLAM data specifically.

title: Europeana Project Month 2026 launches in November
content:
Europeana Project Month 2026 is a series of webinars on the topic of the data space in practice: tools, impact and synergies broadcast during November.

Consisting of 14 projects that Europeana is actively involved in, ECHOES, INFINITY and ECHOLOT will feature in the webinar “Bridging the data space and the ECCCH” and HERITALISE in the webinar “3D Digitisation“.

ECHOES: Building the Cultural Heritage Cloud ecosystem will introduce the project, present the latest progress achieved by ECHOES, and demonstrate how the project is building an open, federated ecosystem that connects institutions, datasets, tools and expertise across Europe. A key focus will be on the relationship between the Cultural Heritage Cloud and the Common European Data Space for Cultural Heritage.

Organised by the Europeana Foundation, the webinars will run every Tuesday and Thursday during November over two sessions:

  • Morning sessions (09:30-12:00 CET)
  • Afternoon sessions (14:00-16:00 CET)

    • Participation is free but registration is required. More information is available on the Data Space website.

title: First ECHOES training course launched on DARIAH-CAMPUS
content:
ECHOES has launched its first training course! Introduction to European Collaborative Cloud for Cultural Heritage aims to build learners’ foundational understanding of the key concepts and technologies necessary to engage with the Cultural Heritage Cloud. The course, available on DARIAH Campus, consists of  five units which provide the background to the development of the ECCCH, the key concepts, how collaboration works in the ECCCH, Open Science and FAIR principles and concludes with a set of illustrative scenarios.

An extract from Unit 2: Key Concepts and Foundations

In addition, ECHOES has also developed the OntoMatchGame to facilitate learning about ontological models. This educational application is in the form of a card game, providing a step-by-step guide to understanding how the ontology works and how mapping is used to associate data with ontology entities.

The training course and OntoMatchGame can both be accessed through the Capacity Building page where further information is also available.
